newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CHRYSLER'S S.AFRICAN SALES DRIVE GETS UNDERWAY.
newsitem.headline: CHRYSLER'S S.AFRICAN SALES DRIVE GETS UNDERWAY.

text.p: Chrysler Corp had sold 50 vehicles in its first month back in South Africa after an absence of more than a decade, senior officials said on Wednesday.
Latin America, Middle East and Africa general manager Ed Brust said this was despite the fact that its new models such as Neon and Cherokee were unknown in the South African market.
"Chrysler is better known for the Valiant, and there are still a lot of models on the road here," public relations manager Evelyn Mariperisena told Reuters.
South Africa is the eighth market Chrysler has re-entered this year after having to pull out of overseas markets in the early 1980s because of financial difficulties.

Announcing the move back to South Africa in June, Chrysler said it initially aimed to sell about 2,500 vehicles a year in South Africa, but that number could grow to nearly 7,500 vehicles by the end of the decade.
Brust said Chrysler had already established dealerships in Johannesburg, Durban, Port Elizabeth and Cape Town and hoped to have about 20 dealers countrywide by the end of 1997.

The right-hand-drive vehicles are being imported fully assembled from Austria and the U.S. and Brust said Chrysler's competitiveness was being aided by South Africa's decision to gradually cut import tariffs to 45 percent from the current 61 percent over four years.
This was, however, counterbalanced by the weaker rand.
"But we have managed to deal with the most recent currency change," he said.
Chrysler was aiming it vehicles at the upper-to- luxury end of the market but was determined to provide quality service.
"We are never going to be South Africa's biggest car franchise but we want to deliver a good product and service," Brust said.
He said it was unlikely that Chrysler would invest in a manufacturing plant in South Africa unless this was warranted by market share.
Chrysler has launched an extensive advertising campaign targetted and has pledged to sponsor black law graduates for internship in leading local corporations to gain experience in commercial law.
